question: Assume today is 2026-10-28. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of cars manufactured in the United Kingdom in September 2026 (total car production for home and export markets, excluding commercial vehicles), as it will be first reported in the Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders' (SMMT) monthly UK car manufacturing release.

target.what: Total number of cars (passenger cars, excluding commercial vehicles) manufactured in the United Kingdom during September 2026, for both home and export markets, as first reported in SMMT's monthly UK car manufacturing release
target.publisher: Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders (SMMT)
target.caveats: Target period is completed relative to cutoff (2026-10-28) but the September 2026 SMMT release may not yet be published at cutoff; the estimate is for the first-reported figure, which may later be revised. Counts factory-gate production of passenger cars (SIC 29.10), not registrations, sales, or com

candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 production is anchored on the same month in prior years (September 2023, 2024, 2025) adjusted for trend and known shocks; September is typically a strong month after the August shutdown.
candidates.data_to_find: SMMT monthly UK car production totals (home + export) for September 2023, 2024, 2025 and the most recent months published before 2026-10-28 (e.g. July/August 2026). Minimum: September values for at least two prior years plus latest YTD.

candidates.hypothesis: YTD 2026 production through August plus a September share of annual output (historically ~9-10% of the year) gives September; or latest monthly run-rate scaled by September seasonal factor.
candidates.data_to_find: SMMT YTD 2026 car production through August 2026, and historical monthly seasonal shares of annual production (September share). Minimum: YTD total and one year of monthly distribution.
search_hints: SMMT UK car production year to date 2026
UK car output January to August 2026

candidates.hypothesis: Total = home + export; export share historically ~75-80%. If export or home figures are reported separately or via trade data, total can be reconstructed.
candidates.data_to_find: SMMT September export and home market car production splits for prior years and any 2026 partial data; alternatively UK car export volumes from trade statistics. Minimum: export share and one component level.
search_hints: SMMT car production export home market September
UK passenger car production home market share

candidates.perspective: UK assembly plants (Nissan Sunderland, Toyota Burnaston, JLR, Mini Oxford, Bentley, etc.)
candidates.hypothesis: Plant-level capacity × utilisation × September operating days approximates national output; plant announcements of volumes, shifts, or shutdowns constrain the total.
candidates.data_to_find: Named UK car plant capacities, 2026 output guidance or shift patterns, and any September 2026 shutdown/restart news. Minimum: aggregate capacity estimate and utilisation signal.
search_hints: UK car plant production 2026 Nissan Sunderland output

candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 output deviates from seasonal norm due to model changeovers, EV mandate effects, plant closures, or supply disruptions; measurable exposure shifts the estimate.
candidates.data_to_find: News of UK car plant stoppages, model launches, or restructuring affecting September 2026 production; SMMT statements on 2026 outlook. Minimum: any dated disruption or boost in Aug-Sep 2026.

candidates.hypothesis: SMMT annual production forecasts or analyst estimates for 2026 can be decomposed to a September figure via seasonal share.
candidates.data_to_find: SMMT 2026 UK car production forecast (annual), and any monthly or quarterly guidance. Minimum: annual forecast figure.

candidates.hypothesis: Steel/aluminium deliveries, component imports, or port vehicle handling for UK-built cars scale with production; a flow ratio bridges to units.
candidates.data_to_find: UK port car handling volumes or component import indices for September 2026; historical ratio of these to car production. Minimum: one flow series with a known conversion.

plan_notes: plan proposed 7 candidate directions in 6 categories; running 7 (budget cap 10)

existing.note: not checked: the existing-figure step runs only in live use with a human at the approval step (not in backtests, scored, --auto-approve or ablation runs)

Currently only scattered months are available.

search_hints: SMMT 'UK car manufacturing' monthly release archive 2025 2026
SMMT motor industry facts monthly production table
tradingeconomics UK car production historical monthly series

directions.hypothesis: Plant-level September 2026 output or shutdown announcements (Nissan Sunderland, JLR, Toyota Burnaston, Mini Oxford, Bentley, McLaren) would constrain the September total and resolve whether the August +6.1% momentum carried into September or reversed after the August shutdown timing shift.
directions.data_to_find: September 2026 production/shutdown/shift announcements at major UK car plants; any SMMT or company statement on September 2026 volumes.

directions.hypothesis: If the September 2026 SMMT release was already published before 2026-10-28, the actual figure would replace all estimates; checking the SMMT release calendar and any pre-cutoff coverage would resolve the target directly.
directions.data_to_find: SMMT UK car manufacturing release for September 2026 (published ~late October 2026) and any news coverage dated on or before 2026-10-28.

methods.rationale: Placeholder structure: scale September 2025 (51,090) by a YoY change factor. However the signal series (August 2026 vs August 2025) is not the same calendar period as the target, so this is better expressed as formula_mc; retained here only if code aligns by year. Primary route is m3.

p125.role: 2026 annual UK car and light vehicle output forecast (740,000 units), used as the annual car production base

a2.role: September share of annual car output

methods.rationale: Annual 2026 forecast (~740k cars/light vehicles) times September's seasonal share (~8.5%). Weakness: p125 is a forecast, not an outcome, and includes light vehicles; the share assumption carries most uncertainty. Provides an independent structural anchor.

p16.role: UK total car production in September 2025 (51,090 units), the base month one year earlier

a1.role: YoY change factor for September 2026 vs September 2025

methods.rationale: Primary route: September 2025 actual (51,090, depressed by the JLR cyber stoppage) scaled by a YoY change factor. The factor is informed by 2026 monthly YoY pattern (Jan -8.2%, May +3.2%, Jul -10.6%, Aug +6.1%, YTD cars -3.9%) and the depressed base. Shared dependency: relies on the single September 2025 SMMT measurement and on the assumed recovery factor; failure mode is that August's +6.1% was a shutdown-timing artefact that reverses in September.

p60.role: UK cumulative passenger car production Jan-Aug 2026 (472,851 cars), the observed partial-year base

a2.role: September share of annual car output

methods.rationale: Alternative structural route: annualise the Jan-Aug 2026 cumulative car output (472,851) and apply September's seasonal share. Uses observed 2026 data rather than a forecast, but annualising 8 months ignores the September seasonal uplift and the August shutdown distortion; the share assumption dominates. Provides a cross-check on m2/m3.

assumptions.name: September 2026 YoY change factor vs September 2025
assumptions.rationale: September 2025 was depressed (51,090, -27.1%) by the JLR cyber stoppage. 2026 monthly YoY has been mixed: Jan -8.2%, Mar -0.8%, Apr -0.7%, May +3.2%, Jun -1.2%, Jul -10.6%, Aug +6.1%; YTD cars -3.9% through August. A modest recovery from the depressed 2025 base is plausible but the sector remains weak (YTD down, model changeovers, EV mandate pressure). Central 1.05 with wide range reflecting uncertainty about whether August momentum persists.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 is compared with September 2025 as the base, and no direct September 2026 observation exists.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 output fell sharply (e.g. a major plant stoppage) or that the August +6.1% was a one-off shutdown-timing artefact that reversed.

assumptions.name: September share of annual car output
assumptions.rationale: September is typically a strong post-August-shutdown month; historically September has been roughly 8-10% of annual UK car output. Using the 2026 annual forecast (~740k-790k cars) times this share gives a September estimate. Central 8.5% with range reflecting seasonal variation.
assumptions.applies_when: A credible 2026 annual car production total is available and September's seasonal share is stable.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 was unusually weak or strong relative to the annual run-rate (e.g. plant shutdowns or surge).

assumptions.name: September 2026 YoY change factor vs September 2025
assumptions.rationale: September 2025 was depressed by the JLR cyber-attack stoppage (p16, p17, p514, p515), so a rebound is plausible. 2026 monthly YoY has been mixed: Jan -8.2%, Feb -10.7%, Mar -0.8%, Apr -0.7%, May +3.2%, Jun -1.2%, Jul -10.6%, Aug +6.1% (p387, p803, p469, p468, p386, p385, p114, p34). YTD cars -3.9% through August (p61). A modest positive factor centred near +5% with wide range reflects the improving trend and easy base, but uncertainty about shutdown timing and model changeovers.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 production is compared with the depressed September 2025 base and the 2026 monthly trend continues.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 output fell sharply (e.g. a major plant stoppage) or that the 2025 base was not depressed.

assumptions.name: September share of annual car output
assumptions.rationale: September is typically a strong post-shutdown month. In 2024, September 70,039 of ~640,000 annual cars (~11%); in 2025, 51,090 of 717,371 (~7.1%). The average is around 8.5-9%, with a range spanning the observed years.
assumptions.applies_when: Annual car output is known or forecast and September follows its usual seasonal share.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026's seasonal share differs materially from the 2024-2025 range.

assumptions.name: September 2026 YoY change factor vs September 2025 (partial-period route)
assumptions.rationale: Same basis as a1: September 2025 was depressed by the JLR stoppage, and 2026 monthly YoY has been mixed but improving (Aug +6.1%, p34). Used to adjust the September 2025 base in the partial-period route.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 production is compared with the depressed September 2025 base.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 output fell sharply or that the 2025 base was not depressed.

assumptions.name: Number of months in the Jan-Aug 2026 cumulative window
assumptions.rationale: Calendar constant: p60 covers January through August 2026, exactly 8 months. Used to convert the cumulative total to a monthly average.
assumptions.applies_when: p60 is the Jan-Aug 2026 cumulative car total.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that p60 covers a different number of months.

methods.label: m1
methods.rationale: Reuse of round-1 route: September 2025 (p16) scaled by the ratio of August 2026 (p33) to September 2025 (p16). This is a weak signal because August and September have different seasonal profiles and the August 2026 figure was distorted by shutdown timing; it is retained as one route but its backtest error will be large.
notes: p16: period 2025-09-01..2025-09-30 is not the same calendar period as 2026-08-01..2026-08-31

methods.label: m3

p16.role: UK total car production in September 2025 (51,090 units), the base month one year earlier

a1.role: YoY change factor for September 2026 vs September 2025

methods.rationale: Reuse of round-1 route: September 2025 base (p16) times a YoY change factor (a1). The base is depressed by the JLR stoppage, so a rebound factor is justified; the wide range reflects uncertainty in the 2026 monthly trend and shutdown timing.

methods.label: m5

p16.role: UK total car production in September 2025 (51,090 units), the base month one year earlier

a3.role: YoY change factor for September 2026 vs September 2025 (partial-period route)

methods.rationale: Alternative YoY route using the same September 2025 base but a separately specified change factor (a3) with the same basis as a1. This is largely redundant with m3 and is included only to reflect the uncertainty in the change factor; code will treat it as overlapping with m3.

weight_basis.m2: B1 of 2 blocks; geometric mean of blocks
weight_basis.m3: B2 of 2 blocks; geometric mean of blocks

combination.weight_gate: off: inverse backtest-error weights need a bank-level gate (>= 30 scored questions with >= 2 backtested routes, hit rate >= 0.7; METHODS_ZH 4.1), which has not been run

m2.note: Monte Carlo width below the default, not used to narrow

m3.note: Monte Carlo width below the default, not used to narrow

interval.rule: several blocks: root mean square of the block widths, times the Birge ratio when it exceeds 1

baseline.rule: seasonal naive: the target's value for the same calendar period last year

excluded_by_input_audit.label: m2
excluded_by_input_audit.reason: input audit: p125: Evidence is a forecast of UK car AND light vehicle output, a broader total than passenger cars only, used as the car production base.

excluded_by_input_audit.label: m4
excluded_by_input_audit.reason: unit check: the formula's result is 'car/(8 month**2)' (car/(8 month) / month * (year/month) * (month/year) = car/(8 month**2)), which is not a 'car' quantity: you judged that it does not fit the target unit 'car': The result is cars per squared month, not a count of cars over a period; dividing by a4 (a count of months) introduces an extra per-month factor, so the unit is not the same kind of quantity as the target car total.

kept.name: September 2026 YoY change factor vs September 2025
kept.rationale: September 2025 was depressed by the JLR cyber-attack stoppage (p16, p17, p514, p515), so a rebound is plausible. 2026 monthly YoY has been mixed: Jan -8.2%, Feb -10.7%, Mar -0.8%, Apr -0.7%, May +3.2%, Jun -1.2%, Jul -10.6%, Aug +6.1% (p387, p803, p469, p468, p386, p385, p114, p34). YTD cars -3.9% t
kept.applies_when: September 2026 production is compared with the depressed September 2025 base and the 2026 monthly trend continues.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 output fell sharply (e.g. a major plant stoppage) or that the 2025 base was not depressed.

kept.name: September share of annual car output
kept.rationale: September is typically a strong post-shutdown month. In 2024, September 70,039 of ~640,000 annual cars (~11%); in 2025, 51,090 of 717,371 (~7.1%). The average is around 8.5-9%, with a range spanning the observed years.
kept.applies_when: Annual car output is known or forecast and September follows its usual seasonal share.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026's seasonal share differs materially from the 2024-2025 range.

kept.name: September 2026 YoY change factor vs September 2025 (partial-period route)
kept.rationale: Same basis as a1: September 2025 was depressed by the JLR stoppage, and 2026 monthly YoY has been mixed but improving (Aug +6.1%, p34). Used to adjust the September 2025 base in the partial-period route.
kept.applies_when: September 2026 production is compared with the depressed September 2025 base.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 output fell sharply or that the 2025 base was not depressed.

kept.name: Number of months in the Jan-Aug 2026 cumulative window
kept.rationale: Calendar constant: p60 covers January through August 2026, exactly 8 months. Used to convert the cumulative total to a monthly average.
kept.applies_when: p60 is the Jan-Aug 2026 cumulative car total.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that p60 covers a different number of months.

The best estimate for total UK car production (passenger cars, home plus export, excluding commercial vehicles) in September 2026 is 53,625 car (80% model-based interval 38,925 to 73,877 car). This is a model-based range conditional on the assumptions, not a demonstrated accuracy guarantee.

The estimate rests on the observed September 2025 base of 51,090 car, scaled by a YoY change factor. September 2025 was depressed by the JLR cyber-attack stoppage, so a rebound is plausible; 2026 monthly YoY has been mixed but improving (August positive). Two routes (53,684 and 53,566 car) use the same base with separately specified factors (1.05, range 0.85 to 1.3; 1.05, range 0.85 to 1.3). Code combined them as overlapping blocks with equal weight, not because they are independent.

The main risk is the assumed rebound factor and 2026 shutdown timing. The most useful missing evidence would be actual September 2026 output or a reliable pre-release signal.

Unit of the estimate: car (total for 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-30).

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a1 September 2026 YoY change factor vs September 2025: 1.05 [n], range 0.85 to 1.3; used by m2. Overturned by: Evidence that September 2026 output fell sharply (e.g. a major plant stoppage) or that the 2025 base was not depressed.
- a3 September 2026 YoY change factor vs September 2025 (partial-period route): 1.05 [n], range 0.85 to 1.3; used by m3. Overturned by: Evidence that September 2026 output fell sharply or that the 2025 base was not depressed.

Method details (computed by code):
- m2 formula_mc: p16 * a1; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 40,718 to 71,279; result unit (car/month) * 1 month converted to car; own 80% width x/÷1.38 (no error evidence, code's default width)
- m3 formula_mc: p16 * a3; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 40,476 to 71,320; result unit (car/month) * 1 month converted to car; own 80% width x/÷1.38 (no error evidence, code's default width)
- Combination: 2 block(s), equal weight per block (methods whose inputs overlap by at least half form one block; backtest errors set widths, not weights): B1 = m2: 53,684 (width x/÷1.38, no error evidence, code's default width); B2 = m3: 53,566 (width x/÷1.38, no error evidence, code's default width). Estimate = the geometric mean of the two blocks.
- Interval: root mean square of the block widths x/÷1.38; Birge ratio 0.01 (not above one, so no widening); final width x/÷1.38.
- Seasonal naive baseline (not combined): 51,090 (2025, from m1); the estimate is +5.0% against it.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
